output.myth: Kael the Netter cast for fallen stars every night and never once hauled one up. One night the net came back heavy and wet, and in it was a gull, the first she had ever caught. Kael's hands shook, because the mesh had her by the wing and she would not stop beating. He thought of Hesk at the pole, who keeps count of every thing that is taken, and he thought of the fallen star still falling somewhere past the Lamp Road. So he loosed the knot, one thread at a time, and let her go. Tavo took her up at once, laughing, and she went off over the Windward Reach with a square of net still tangled in her wing. She is up there now. Look for her when the wind is right: she goes back and forth between the lamps, and the knot-mark shows pale on her wing. Kael still casts. He comes home, empty-handed.
output.verse:
Net-knot on her wing
she tacks back and forth in wind
Kael still casts for stars
